name: Bow
description: One string, three ways to play it: plucked, held singing by an ebow, or bowed. Sustained guitar swells and cello-like drones from a waveguide string with a resonant body.

params.name: Mode
params.description: How the string is played: plucked and left to ring, held singing by an ebow, or bowed with a rosin edge. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Attack
params.description: How long an ebowed or bowed note takes to bloom. On Pluck it is a volume swell over the pick, switched off at the shortest setting.

params.name: Release
params.description: How long the string rings on after the key is released. It never rings longer than Decay.

params.name: Brightness
params.description: How long the upper partials ring, from a dull, damped string to a bright, wiry one. It also brightens the pick, the ebow and the bow.

params.name: Decay
params.description: How long a plucked string rings while its key is held. It also limits how long any note rings after release.

params.name: Position
params.description: Where along the string it is played, from thin and bright near the bridge to rounder and hollow towards the middle. Clearest on Pluck.

params.name: Pressure
params.description: How hard the ebow or bow presses: the ebow moves towards the octave, the bow from flute-like to raspy. Pluck ignores it.

params.name: Body
params.description: How much of the instrument's resonant body is heard. More adds low and mid resonances and takes away some of the bare string.

params.name: Vibrato
params.description: Depth of the pitch vibrato. It fades in a moment after each note starts.

params.name: Detune
params.description: Tunes each note's two strings apart, left and right, so they beat slowly, or leaves one string at zero. Applies from the next note.

params.name: Volume
params.description: Output level of the instrument. A soft clip after it rounds off the peaks when many notes stack up.

origin.note: Written for live-mix on cpp/kit. A two-segment digital waveguide string (Karplus-Strong and Jaffe-Smith lineage) with the excitation at the junction. The ebow and the bow share one driver: it reads the string's own fundamental, pushes in phase with it to hold a set level, and adds upper partials from a table read at the string's phase (the octave for a hard-driven ebow, a slipping-string ramp plus rosin noise for the bow). A friction-junction bow was tried and dropped because it fell into double-slip and whistling regimes. Not a model of a particular instrument.
